result.reasoning:
The raise is real at the raw-kernel level but it is not a defect: it is the engine-wide contract, it is structurally unreachable, and it cannot change any number or conclusion.

1. The literal crash reproduces (scripts in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/refute-csrz-zerowidth/). `ops_ext.cs_robust_z(torch.zeros((2,0)))` -> `IndexError: median(): Expected reduction dim 1 to have non-zero size.` The reporter's control case is also right: `cs_robust_z(torch.full((1,9), nan))` returns all-NaN, `(1,1)` returns 0.0, `(0,9)` (zero DAYS) returns `(0,9)` cleanly. So only a zero-LENGTH stock axis raises.

2. It is NOT a Partura deviation -- upstream AlphaCube's own kernel does exactly the same. I ran all 27 cs-family kernels in the registry on a `(2,0)` panel (compare_builtins.py). Four fail, and one of them is read-only upstream: `alphacube/operators/nd_cs.py::cs_median` -> the IDENTICAL `IndexError: median(): Expected reduction dim 1 to have non-zero size.` (it shares `common._median` = `x.nanmedian(dim=-1).values`, /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/operators/common.py:395-396). `cs_quantile` (upstream) and `cs_winsor` (Partura) also fail. So "degrade gracefully on a zero-length stock axis" is not the house convention; `cs_robust_z` matches the reference implementation it is modeled on. Fixing only Partura's copy would make it diverge from the engine kernel it is meant to mirror.

3. A zero-length stock axis is structurally unreachable (reachability.py, all four gates run for real):
   - G1: the single place any view is built, `CubeStore.view` (/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/store.py:216-217), has an explicit guard `if sym_idx.size == 0: raise ValueError("no symbols selected")`. Verified: `store.view(max_symbols=0)` raises, and so does `warmed_view(store, None, None, 10, max_symbols=0)` -- which is the exact call `PanelSet.__init__` makes (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/panels.py:162). So `--max-symbols 0` fails loudly at setup, long before a kernel runs.
   - G2: the `--data store` segmented path shares that guard verbatim: `SegmentedCubeStore.view is CubeStore.view` -> True (store.py:393, `view = CubeStore.view`). Partura never constructs a `CubeView` itself and never passes an explicit `symbols=` list (only `max_symbols`), so there is no second route in.
   - G3: the engine's chunk loop `for lo in range(0, n, step); hi = min(lo+step, n)` (engine.py:176-178) with `step = max(1, ...)` never emits an empty slice -- checked for n in {0,1,6,5000} x step in {1,7,1e9}: zero empty chunks in every case (at n=0 no chunk runs at all). And cs kernels are not chunked on the stock axis anyway.
   - G4: the only place in the codebase that hands kernels arbitrary shapes, the probe harness, already degrades on its own: `probes.run_probes` wraps every probe in try/except and records `{"error": ...}` (partura/probes.py:183-186). `semantics.dossier("cs_robust_z", shape=(4,0))` does not crash -- it returns a dossier with 4 probes carrying the IndexError as a string. Default probe shapes are `(40,24)` / `(16,241)` and are only ever grown with `max(...)`, never shrunk.
   - The external-panel loader is also sealed: `PanelSet.external` rejects anything whose shape != `(len(self.dates), len(self.symbols))` (panels.py:258-259), and that view is non-empty by G1.

4. End-to-end evidence on what the kernel really sees (e2e_shapes.py): with a spy installed in the registry before the catalog is built, `evaluate_factors(store, {"f": "cs_robust_z(day_mean(Close))"})` on a 6-symbol x 40-day synthetic store calls `cs_robust_z` exactly once with the full panel `(40, 6)` = (days, stocks), identically at `chunk_symbols` = None / 1 / 2. The stock axis is never sliced for a cs kernel (it is a MODE_P panel round), so the minimum last-dim ever reached equals `n_symbols`, which the G1 guard forces to be >= 1.

5. Scope: even in the hypothetical, the behaviour is a loud exception, not a silently wrong value -- it cannot shift a Sharpe, an excess return, a half-life pick or a selection verdict. Under the review mandate (only report defects that change numbers or conclusions) this does not qualify. The reporter's own write-up concedes the input is unreachable and the evidence field is empty.

result.reproduction:
Reproduced the literal raise but NOT an erroneous result, and not through any reachable path.

(a) Raw kernel, as reported -- raise confirmed:
    ALPHACUBE_ROOT=/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube PYTHONPATH=/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src:/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura ~/.venvs/alphacube/bin/python repro.py
    CASE zero-width (2,0): RAISED IndexError: median(): Expected reduction dim 1 to have non-zero size.
    CASE all-NaN width 9 (1,9): NO CRASH -> all NaN
    CASE width 1 (1,1): NO CRASH -> [0.0]
    CASE zero-days (0,9): NO CRASH -> shape (0,9)

(b) Same raise from UPSTREAM AlphaCube's own kernel, so this is the engine's contract, not a Partura bug:
    --- cs-family kernels that CRASH on a (2,0) panel: 4 ---
      [alphacube] cs_median      IndexError: median(): Expected reduction dim 1 to have non-zero size.
      [alphacube] cs_quantile    TypeError (missing quantile arg)
      [PARTURA  ] cs_robust_z    IndexError: median(): Expected reduction dim 1 to have non-zero size.
      [PARTURA  ] cs_winsor      RuntimeError: quantile() input tensor must be non-empty
    --- survive (2,0): 23 ---

(c) Could not reach it from the pipeline -- every gate blocks it:
    G1 store.view(max_symbols=0)            -> RAISES ValueError: no symbols selected
    G1 warmed_view(..., max_symbols=0)      -> RAISES ValueError: no symbols selected   [the call PanelSet makes]
    G1 store.view(max_symbols=None)         -> n_symbols=6
    G2 SegmentedCubeStore.view is CubeStore.view: True
    G3 (n_symbols, step, n_chunks, n_EMPTY_chunks) for n in {0,1,6,5000} x step in {1,7,1e9}: n_EMPTY_chunks = 0 in all 12 combinations
    G4 semantics.dossier("cs_robust_z", shape=(4,0)) did NOT crash; 4 probes reported the IndexError as a string
    G4 semantics.dossier("cs_robust_z") (default shape (40,24)): 0 errors

(d) What the engine actually passes the kernel (spy in the registry, synthetic 6-symbol x 40-day store):
    chunk_symbols=None -> cs_robust_z called with (40, 6); min last-dim 6
    chunk_symbols=1    -> cs_robust_z called with (40, 6); min last-dim 6
    chunk_symbols=2    -> cs_robust_z called with (40, 6); min last-dim 6
    i.e. always the full (days, stocks) panel, last dim == n_symbols >= 1 by G1.
